newsitem.title: FRANCE: French reinsurer Scor 1996 profits surge.
newsitem.headline: French reinsurer Scor 1996 profits surge.

text.p: Leading French reinsurer Scor reported on Thursday that 1996 profits climbed 20 percent and surprised the stock market by doubling its dividend.

Scor, one of the world's largest providers of reinsurance to property-casualty and life insurers, reported net attributable profit rose to 624 million francs ($107.9 million), up from 522 million and increased its net dividend to 10 francs from five.
Net earned premiums rose to 10.40 billion francs from 9.30 billion.
Investors welcomed Scor's performance, driving up shares 2.82 percent by early afternoon to 244.0 francs.
The company was also upbeat on prospects for 1997.
"The start of 1997 looks pretty good," Scor chairman Jacques Blondeau told financial analysts.
"We don't see any reason why 1997 should be very different from 1996," he said, but declined to say whether the profit jump would match that of 1996.

Blondeau said that while the industry "had experienced major consolidation and rate pressure in some areas, we have prospered by continuing to expand our global reach and by concentrating on higher margin segments of the reinsurance industry".
He said that the company had been "particularly satisfied" by the results of its life reinsurance business.
The reinsurer, which listed its shares on Wall Street last year, said it aimed to maintain a return on equity of between 10 and 12 percent. It stood at 11.3 percent in 1996.
The company said a slight deterioration in technical conditions should be offset by a fall in costs and a five percent rise in business in 1997.
Blondeau said that the decision to double the dividend reflected a somewhat exceptional situation.
Unlike U.S. reinsurers which can carry out share buybacks, which involves tax disadvantages in France, Scor decided to pay out a higher dividend to reward shareholders, he said.
Blondeau said he believed the current wave of consolidation in the reinsurance sector would diminish its cyclical nature.
He said he did not rule out acquisitions this year as part of the consolidation process but said they would only be carried under "reasonable financial conditions".
The French group bought last July the reinsurance portfolio of U.S. insurer Allstate. ($ = 5.781 French Francs)
